challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: Regarding the nightly pipeline bottleneck, I am prepared to accept a manual data versioning step to keep the morning order window open. I will give up the automated lineage tracking for the next release cycle if the underlying data remains fully backed up and recoverable. This trade allows us to ship the reliability fix without waiting for the infrastructure budget approval. I am not asking for a permanent regression to manual handling, only a temporary bridge while we secure the validation layer. The priority is ensuring store managers see a valid forecast before the till opens, even if the versioning log is compiled by hand for a few weeks.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up automated lineage tracking in exchange for keeping the morning order window open, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
